messages:
Maria G: Heads up — need a short cross-team sync on GPU SM occupancy, per-GPU memory headroom, and queue depth for both Hosted + Dedicated pools. PM wants a capacity dashboard and an alerting plan.
AJ: Scope: do we want per-instance (VM/GPU) metrics or just aggregated pool-level? per-tenant for Dedicated?
Maria G: Ideally both. Pool-level for SLOs, per-instance for on-call/debug and Dedicated customer chargeback. But watch cardinality.
Kai L: Proposed metric names to start: `redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_ratio{gpu_id, pool}`, `redwood_gpu_mem_used_bytes{gpu_id, pool}`, `redwood_gpu_queue_depth{pool}`. Keep labels limited: pool, region, tenant_id (only for Dedicated, optional).
Jordan P: Strong +1 on limited labels. If we emit `pod`, `container`, `model_name` we explode cardinality. Suggest a `tenant_id` label that's hashed/low-card for Dedicated billing only.
Tess R: For Hosted, we should not add tenant labels at GPU level. Instead emit `route`/`customer_tier` at request-level and use tracing to tie back when needed. Aggregation rollups hourly/daily for chargeback.
AJ: PromQL examples?
Kai L: Example pool-level SM occupancy: `sum by (pool) (sm_occupied_tokens_total) / sum by (pool) (sm_capacity_tokens_total)` — or use a gauge `redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_ratio`. For queue depth: `sum by (pool) (redwood_gpu_queue_depth)` and 95p: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, pool) (redwood_gpu_queue_depth_bucket))`.
Maria G: Nice. How do we define `sm_capacity_tokens_total` — per GPU hardware-dependent? Need mapping table for A100 vs H100.
Kai L: Yes. Runtime can report a `gpu_model` label once per exporter scrape; capacity computed from a small lookup in metrics pipeline. We'll publish `sm_capacity_tokens_total` as a gauge exported by node-exporter variant.
Jordan P: Concern: scraping per-GPU on every host at 5s will create ~N*Q metrics. For Hosted fleets that's big. Propose 15s scrape plus a push gateway for Dedicated autoscaled nodes.
Tess R: Also need a low-cardinality derived metric for dashboards. In telemetry pipeline create `pool:sm_occupancy:avg_1m` and `pool:queue_depth:p95_1m`. Those are what consoles/dashboard should use.
AJ: Alerts — suggested thresholds?
Maria G: For now: `pool:sm_occupancy:avg_1m > 0.92` warning, `>0.98` critical. Queue depth p95 > 20 requests -> warning. Memory free < 8% -> critical for H100. Need per-hardware tuning.
Kai L: + add an alert that fires only if both occupancy high and queue depth rising to avoid noise. Example: `increase(pool:queue_depth:sum[2m]) > 5 and pool:sm_occupancy:avg_1m > 0.95`.
infra-bot: deploy/telemetry-metrics check — new metric `redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_ratio` detected in staging exporters.
Maria G: Good catch infra-bot. Who owns the telemetry schema and dashboard PR?
Tess R: I'll own the dashboard panels and alert rules. Kai can own the exporter/Prometheus side. Jordan can validate SRE paging logic.
Jordan P: I'll draft SLO/alert runbook snippets and add escalation.
AJ: I'll coordinate with Product for Dedicated chargeback fields (tenant_id hashing).
Maria G: Action items summarized: (1) Kai: exporter + capacity lookup PR, (2) Tess: Grafana panels + alert rules using rollups, (3) Jordan: runbook + pagerplay, (4) AJ: product mapping for Dedicated. Add tickets in telemetry repo and link here. Target: demo in next eng sync. :thumbsup:
Kai L: I'll open exporter PR and add perf numbers for 15s vs 5s scraping.
Tess R: I'll prototype a dashboard JSON and drop it in `grafana/dashboards/prototypes` branch.
Maria G: Thanks all — let's keep follow-ups in this thread and tag infra-bot when PRs merge.
